properties.line: Norwich and Worcester: Worcester – Allyn's Point
properties.speed_source: estimated, blended across the line's history; unsourced

segments.note: Chartered 1832 in Connecticut and 1833 in Massachusetts, the two companies merged in June 1836; construction began Nov 1835. The line opened Norwich-Plainfield in Sept 1839 and reached Worcester on Mar 9 1840, following the Shetucket, Quinebaug, and French River valleys through Griswold, Plainfield, Killingly, Putnam, and Thompson (CT) and Webster, Oxford, and Auburn (MA). At Norwich it connected with steamships (the railroad's own Worcester and New York) running down the Thames River and Long Island Sound to New York City -- the famous 'Norwich Line,' a boat-train route that avoided the cost of building rail along the irregular Connecticut shoreline. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: A 6-mile extension south from Norwich along the east bank of the Thames River to Allyn's Point, completed Dec 1843, gave the Norwich Line year-round steamboat connections -- the upper river above Norwich iced over most winters, stranding the boats. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Local passenger service was revived June 9 1952 using a Budd Rail Diesel Car, running two daily round trips (later three). It ended April 30 1971, the day before Amtrak's national takeover -- this route was not included in the new Amtrak system, and no passenger train has served Norwich since. Providence and Worcester Railroad, which had operated the northern half since 1976, purchased the entire line from Conrail in 1980 and still runs freight over it today as its 'Norwich Branch.'
